name: Rosy Retrospection
description: People often remember past experiences as better than they felt in the moment. Memory polishes the past, so the remembered version can become more positive than the live experience actually was.
design_relevance_note: Directly relevant to retrospective UX research, churn/win-back interviews, season-end journey reviews, and delayed NPS or satisfaction studies: users and teams may praise the remembered journey while underweighting the friction that was present during the real interaction.
prevalence_note: Well known in memory and experience-evaluation research, and useful in UX-research interpretation, but not a routine named law in everyday product-design pattern libraries.

findings.description: Across longitudinal evaluations of lived experiences, retrospective memories became more positive than evaluations recorded closer to the experience itself: people later remembered the past as better than it felt in the moment, producing a 'rosy view' of prior events.
findings.source_title: Temporal Adjustments in the Evaluation of Events: The “Rosy View”
